title: Effectiveness of Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) with Batfish for LLM-generated vendor CLI configurations — preregistered design (repaired)
research_question: Does a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline that uses an LLM for config generation, Batfish as a deterministic verifier plus a secondary automated checker, and an automated LLM-based repair loop reduce verifier-detected semantic/safety failures compared to plain LLM generation for vendor-specific network configuration tasks?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: The GVR pipeline (LLM generation + Batfish verification + automated repair loop) yields a higher paired success rate (proportion of tasks passing verifier checks after GVR) than direct LLM outputs (paired estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline > 0).

H2: For the planned task set, the median number of automated repair iterations required to reach a Batfish pass is < 5 and the median end-to-end (generation→verification→repair→final-verify) latency per task remains within the preregistered operational bound (median ≤ 60 s).
exploratory_questions: EQ1: How do failure-mode reductions (syntax vs semantic vs reachability) distribute across vendor families (Cisco-like vs Juniper-like)?
EQ2: How sensitive are paired outcomes to prompt perturbations (published frozen prompt ± small controlled perturbations)?
EQ3: What fraction of tasks are flagged as potentially contaminated by provenance overlap with public corpora (contamination sensitivity analysis)?
benchmark_scope: Public NetConfEval-style intent→CLI tasks (publicly available examples) plus deterministic synthetic task generator for coverage gaps
Two vendor-CLI families: Cisco-like and Juniper-like (synthetic dialects derived from public vendor docs)
Synthetic topologies (deterministically seeded) representative of small-to-medium enterprise networks (10–50 devices) generated by the published topology generator
sampling_plan: Confirmatory paired design with N=300 independent intents (task pairs). Tasks are generated deterministically from: (a) public NetConfEval-style examples (≥150 items) and (b) synthetic generator seeded RNG (≥150 items) to reach 300 total. Two vendor clusters: Cisco-like (150 tasks) and Juniper-like (150 tasks). Each intent yields one baseline LLM output and one GVR pipeline execution (GVR includes initial generation plus at most one guarded repair call). Task cluster count = 2 (vendors). All seeds, generator code, and dataset provenance will be published. Inclusion: public-sourceable tasks or synthetic tasks generated by the published generator. Exclusion: tasks whose intended semantics cannot be represented in the synthetic topologies; deterministic exclusion rules implemented in code and logged. Confirmatory items (pair count) = 300. Per the registered adapter contract, exactly one initial model generation is produced per task (shared_initial_candidate) and, if deterministic validation fails, at most one guarded repair call is made. Runtime model-sampling parameters will be recorded during execution; nondeterministic sampling is possible and not claimed to be eliminated.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Target: detect a 0.10 absolute increase in pass-rate with 80% power at α=0.05 (two-sided) using paired-proportion assumptions. Conservative recommended N=300 pairs selected after sensitivity analysis across baseline pass-rates 0.30–0.50. Secondary power sensitivity analyses (bootstrap) will report achieved power given observed discordant-pair rates. Recommended budget scenario: 'recommended' (N=300).
exclusion_rules: Exact-public-duplicate tasks detected by provenance cross-check are excluded from primary confirmatory analysis.

Pairs where model generation for either condition fails due to transient infrastructure errors will be retried up to 2 automatic retries per failed call; if retries exhausted, handle according to missingness_plan (see below).
Tasks whose intended semantics cannot be represented in the deterministic synthetic topology generator are excluded by deterministic code rules; all exclusions logged and hashed.
missingness_plan: Technical LLM/API failures and verifier crashes are logged with deterministic failure codes. Retry policy: up to 2 automatic retries per failed model call. Primary treatment: 'complete_pair_primary' (pairs with genuine infrastructure/model API failures are excluded from primary test only if exclusionary failure provenance indicates an infrastructure error that equally affected both arms). Sensitivity analysis: 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' treats missing model outputs as failures (zero) for conservative bounds. All retries, failures, and exclusions are fully logged and hashed for reproducibility.
analysis_plan: Confirmatory analysis executed by the registered 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' executor. Primary analysis: paired test of verifier pass-rate difference (GVR final pass vs baseline initial pass) using the executor's McNemar/paired-proportion method, estimator id 'paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline'. Report exact paired p-value and 95% confidence interval for the paired difference. Failed-call treatment (primary): 'complete_pair_primary' (per registered analysis contract). Sensitivity analysis: 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity'. Secondary analyses: Wilcoxon signed-rank for latency and median repair iterations; stratified analyses by vendor and failure-mode. Bonferroni correction applied to at most 3 secondary estimand tests.
multiplicity_plan: Primary estimand tested at α=0.05. Secondary estimands (median iterations, median latency, failure-mode stratified differences) use Bonferroni-adjusted significance thresholds (α_adjusted = 0.05 / number_of_secondary_tests) for formal tests. Exploratory analyses labeled as exploratory and not used to support primary claims.
contamination_plan: {"benchmark_names": ["NetConfEval-like public examples (public provenance)", "Deterministic synthetic task generator (published artifacts)"], "risk_factors": ["Training-data overlap between the hosted LLM and public NetConf examples", "Synthetic generator producing items identical to public corpus examples"], "detection_procedures": ["Provenance cross-check: exact-string and fuzzy-match against publicly indexed corpora to flag near-duplicates", "Automated n-gram overlap score and heuristics to flag likely contamination (preregistered thresholds)", "Secondary check: for flagged items, run alternate prompts (perturbation) and compare outputs for overfitting signals"], "item_flagging_rules": ["If exact match to a public example → flag as 'duplicate_public' and exclude from primary confirmatory analysis (retained only in exploratory contamination-rate reports)", "If fuzzy-match overlap > threshold → flag as 'likely_overlap' and include in sensitivity analyses only"], "analysis_treatment": "Primary analysis excludes exact-public-duplicates. Sensitivity analyses report results including flagged items and treating flagged items as separate subgroup.", "residual_uncertainty": ["Remaining probability that hosted LLM memorized unseen public configs but does not produce identical outputs (undetectable contamination)", "Coverage gaps in public corpora indexing leading to false negatives in detection"]}
stopping_rule: No interim stopping for efficacy or futility. Execute confirmatory N=300 pairs as preregistered. Technical halting allowed only for documented infrastructure failures requiring recovery; any deviation logged and disclosed. Per registered adapter, task selection indices are fixed before model outcomes and not changed based on observed performance.
planned_outputs: Paired analysis results (primary estimand point estimate, 95% CI, exact p-value)
Secondary analyses (median repair iterations, median latency, stratified differences)
Raw model outputs, verification logs, transformation artifacts, and hashed execution manifest
Full reproducible code and dataset provenance
Five-page IEEE-formatted manuscript and disclosure statement
